chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: The friendly Look review of Selections from the Gutter
summary: Hodes says Feather wrote a complimentary Look review of the Gutter record, probably arranged by Milt Gabler before the argument.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: But you don't know the worst part about it. Let me tell you the worst part, which will go in the book. Is, I got a writeup in Look magazine, and I still have that, in which he reviewed Selections From the Gutter. And it was a very complimentary thing.

The record. He says, a sincere piano solo by Art Hodes, Russian-born Art Hodes. Blues flavor and all that. There wasn't a bad thing there. He doesn't say I'm a great pianistic pianist. But there's nothing bad about the rendition.

I think -- it's my opinion that Milt Gabler, who was putting it out on Commodore, got Leonard to do this, and they inserted it. There was ten records reviewed. Mine was the bottom one, by Look. And I don't know if this is true, but I think that it was Milt that got him to do this. This was pre-argument, before this thing.
